objective: Test whether the portfolio turns a deep, public-safe record into timely hiring understanding, corroborated role evidence, complete operating narratives, current proof, inspectable artifacts, exact-commit release discipline, and a maintainable evaluation practice.

criteria.label: Hiring-reader comprehension
criteria.intent: A time-limited hiring reader can identify Jamie's role, operating contribution, proof, resume, and contact path; automation may prepare the test but only real reader sessions can earn 5.

anchors.1: The audience and task are undefined or the role must be reconstructed.
anchors.3: A repeatable protocol exists, but route evidence or task coverage is incomplete.
anchors.4: Five bounded task cases and deterministic route evidence are ready; real hiring-reader sessions remain open.
anchors.5: At least five privacy-safe real reader sessions meet the comprehension target and their aggregate findings inform the site.

criteria.label: Collaborator corroboration
criteria.intent: The five highest-value role-attribution gaps have consent-aware proof requests and cannot be represented as corroborated until collaborators actually respond.

anchors.1: Role gaps are implicit or self-assertion is treated as collaborator proof.
anchors.3: Five prioritized requests, questions, boundaries, and publication permissions are ready; no response is invented.
anchors.4: At least three target projects have usable collaborator proof notes with explicit permission states.
anchors.5: All five target projects have bounded corroboration integrated into the knowledge lifecycle.

criteria.label: End-to-end operating narratives
criteria.intent: At least three flagship projects connect condition, diagnosis, intervention, coordination, changed behavior, outcome, evidence, and limits without inflating causality.

anchors.1: Projects list activity without explaining Jamie's operating contribution or what changed.
anchors.3: Some causal steps are visible, but evidence, outcome, or collective boundaries are incomplete.
anchors.4: Three complete evidence-linked sequences exist with bounded outcomes.
anchors.5: The three sequences are complete, route-aligned, independently inspectable, and resistant to sole-causation drift.

criteria.label: Current 2024-2026 evidence
criteria.intent: Current practice is visible through at least three bounded records, including source-backed work and repository-verifiable implementation, without relabeling a proposal as delivered client work.

anchors.1: The portfolio depends almost entirely on older projects or treats recent preparation as delivered impact.
anchors.3: Recent work is named but scattered, weakly sourced, or absent from an intentional evidence layer.
anchors.4: Three current-practice records are normalized with sources, public surfaces, and boundaries.
anchors.5: Three or more recent records include externally corroborated outcomes and decisive public artifacts.

criteria.label: Consent-cleared visual proof
criteria.intent: Real work becomes inspectable through cleared artifacts while unapproved photographs, participants, private records, and proprietary material remain excluded.

anchors.1: The site has no inspectable work or publishes material without clearance.
anchors.3: One cleared artifact is live and a rights-aware multi-project selection queue exists.
anchors.4: At least two flagship cases have cleared, source-backed visual evidence.
anchors.5: At least three flagship cases have decisive, accessible, rights-cleared visual proof.

criteria.label: Exact-SHA production evidence
criteria.intent: Repository checks, staging review, accessibility, Docker, approval, deployment, and production smoke evidence stay attached to one exact SHA; a branch pass cannot impersonate a release.

anchors.1: Readiness is inferred from a nearby branch, stale report, or unrecorded deployment.
anchors.3: The complete exact-SHA protocol and commands exist; no unperformed release action is marked complete.
anchors.4: One exact candidate SHA has complete local, Docker, staging, and accessibility evidence plus Jamie's approval.
anchors.5: That same SHA is promoted and passes documented production smoke verification.

criteria.label: Evaluation and source maintenance
criteria.intent: Named ownership, review cadence, source-health checks, complexity limits, retirement rules, and anti-self-certification keep the system useful beyond the agent that created it.

anchors.1: The system has no owner, cadence, freshness policy, or complexity limit.
anchors.3: Maintenance is documented but lacks enforceable freshness or anti-gaming controls.
anchors.4: Ownership, cadence, source health, complexity budget, and retirement rules are explicit and checked.
anchors.5: The policy is current, deterministic, independently reviewable, and integrated into the root verification gate.

antiGaming: An LLM, browser script, or repository source check is not a real hiring-reader session.
A Jamie-authored memory, AI archive review, press mention, or shared-account post is not a collaborator proof note.
Activity, outreach, response counts, appropriations, and proposals must not be converted into adoption, attendance, receipt, implementation, or impact.
A visual candidate cannot count as cleared until rights, people, crop, credit, source, and publication context are approved.
A passing branch, rebuilt image, or nearby commit cannot substitute for the exact staging-reviewed and approved production SHA.
Do not improve maintainability by deleting difficult criteria, guardrails, protected absences, or unresolved external gates.

objectiveOrder: make every blind spot measurable without overstating current evidence
raise every criterion to its local evidence floor
raise the weighted score without converting external work into self-certified completion
preserve explicit next evidence needed for every score below 5
hillClimb.stopWhen: Every criterion meets its minimum and the weighted target passes twice consecutively; scores below 5 remain explicit external work queues, not hidden failures.
